title: WOKVAC Vaccine to Prevent Brain Metastases in Metastatic HER2 Positive Breast Cancer, SHIELD Trial
official: A Single-Arm, Phase II Trial: Study of HER2+ Metastatic Breast Cancer Immunization to Enable CNS Lesion Defense (SHIELD)
summary: This phase II trial tests how well the WOKVAC vaccine works in preventing brain metastases in patients with HER2 positive, hormone receptor negative or low breast cancer that has spread from where it first started (primary site) to other places in the body (metastatic). WOKVAC is a vaccine made from tumor-associated proteins, pUMVC3, IGFBP2, HER2, and IGF1R, and may help the body build an effective immune response to kill tumor cells. Sargramostim is a substance that helps make more white blood cells, especially granulocytes, macrophages, and cells that become platelets It is a cytokine that is a type of hematopoietic (blood forming) agent. Giving WOKVAC mixed with sargramostim may help prevent the development of brain metastases in patients with HER2 positive, hormone receptor negative or metastatic breast cancer.
conditions: Anatomic Stage IV Breast Cancer AJCC v8
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participants must be at least ≥ 18 years of age
* Histologically confirmed HER2-positive on metastatic tumor tissue by immunohistochemistry (IHC) or by fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), in accordance with American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO)/College of American Pathologists (CAP) guidelines for HER2 testing
* Hormone receptor negative/low on metastatic tumor tissue, if available (primary tumor tissue can be used if metastatic biopsy tissue cannot be obtained)

  * Estrogen receptor (ER): ≤ 10 % positive tumor cell nuclei and/or
  * Progesterone receptor (PR): ≤ 10% positive tumor cell nuclei
* Diagnosed with metastatic disease no more than 24 months prior to enrollment
* No evidence of brain metastases on contrast-enhanced MRI within 60 days prior to first vaccine
* Receiving first- or second-line standard systemic therapy for metastatic disease. Induction + maintenance regimens (e.g., docetaxel + trastuzumab and pertuzumab \[HP\] followed by HP alone may be counted together as first line)
* Clinically and radiographically stable disease on most recent restaging, performed ≤ 90 days prior to consent
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0 or 1
* White blood cell ≥ 2.0 THOU/uL (prior to first vaccine)
* Lymphocyte count ≥ 0.5 THOU/uL (prior to first vaccine)
* Absolute neutrophil count ≥ 0.7 THOU/uL (prior to first vaccine)
* Platelets ≥ 75 THOU/uL (prior to first vaccine)
* Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x institutional upper limit of normal, except participants with Gilbert's syndrome in whom total bilirubin must be \< 3.0 mg/d (prior to first vaccine)
* Aspartate aminotransferase (AST)/alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤ 3 x institutional upper limit of normal (prior to first vaccine)
* Creatinine ≤ 2.0 mg/dL or creatinine clearance \> 30 mL/min (prior to first vaccine)
* At least 30 days post systemic steroids prior to first vaccine, unless used as part of prophylaxis to prevent intravenous (IV) contrast reactions.

  * Topical, ocular, intra-articular, intranasal, inhalational corticosteroids (with minimal systemic absorption) are allowed
* Must have recovered from major infections and/or surgical procedures; and in the opinion of the investigator, not have any significant active concurrent medical illnesses or condition precluding protocol treatment

Exclusion Criteria:

* Known or suspected CNS metastatic disease
* Prior HER2-targeted vaccine therapy or participation in another HER2-targeted vaccine trial
* Active uncontrolled intercurrent illness or infection
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding
* Current investigational anticancer therapy
* Major surgery within 4 weeks prior to first vaccination
* Known hypersensitivity to WOKVAC and/or vaccine adjuvant components
* Uncontrolled or significant cardiac disease, including symptomatic restrictive or dilated cardiomyopathy, unstable angina within 4 months, New York Heart Association (NYHA) class III-IV heart failure on active treatment, or symptomatic pericardial effusion
* Inability to comply with protocol-specified timing restrictions for non-study vaccinations (i.e., administration within 14 days before or after WOKVAC dosing)
